questions.q: The monthly sales of a product from January to April were 120, 135, 150 and 165 units, respectively. The cost price of the product was Rs. 240 per unit, and a fixed marked price was used for the product in all the four months. Discounts of 20%, 10% and 5% were given on the marked price per unit in January, February and March, respectively, while no discounts were given in April. If the total profit from January to April was Rs. 138825, then the marked price per unit, in rupees, was
questions.solution: Total units are 570, costing ₹136800. Required sales revenue is ₹275625. Discount-weighted units are 120×0.8+135×0.9+150×0.95+165=525. Marked price =275625/525=₹525.

questions.q: Teams A, B, and C consist of five, eight, and ten members, respectively, such that every member within a team is equally productive. Working separately, teams A, B, and C can complete a certain job in 40 hours, 50 hours, and 4 hours, respectively. Two members from team A, three members from team B, and one member from team C together start the job, and the member from team C leaves after 23 hours. The number of additional member(s) from team B, that would be required to replace the member from team C, to finish the job in the next one hour, is
questions.solution: Individual hourly rates in A,B,C are 1/200,1/400,1/40. Initial joint rate is 2/200+3/400+1/40=17/400. After 23 hours, remaining work is 9/400. The original A and B members provide 7/400 per hour. Two additional B members supply the missing 2/400.

questions.q: In a school with 1500 students, each student chooses any one of the streams out of science, arts, and commerce, by paying a fee of Rs 1100, Rs 1000, and Rs 800, respectively. The total fee paid by all the students is Rs 15,50,000. If the number of science students is not more than the number of arts students, then the maximum possible number of science students in the school is
questions.solution: Let science,arts,commerce counts be s,a,c. Subtract ₹1000 per student from the total fee: 100s−200c=50000, so s=500+2c. Then a=1000−3c. The condition s≤a gives c≤100; maximum s=700.

questions.q: In an arithmetic progression, if the sum of fourth, seventh and tenth terms is 99, and the sum of the first fourteen terms is 497, then the sum of first five terms is
questions.solution: The fourth, seventh and tenth terms sum to three times the seventh term, so a+6d=33. Also 7(2a+13d)=497, giving 2a+13d=71. Thus d=5 and a=3. Sum of five terms =5(2×3+4×5)/2=65.

questions.q: Ankita walks from A to C through B, and runs back through the same route at a speed that is 40% more than her walking speed. She takes exactly 3 hours 30 minutes to walk from B to C as well as to run from B to A. The total time, in minutes, she would take to walk from A to B and run from B to C, is
questions.solution: Running speed is 1.4 times walking speed. Since walking BC and running BA each take 210 minutes, walking AB takes 294 and running BC takes 150. The required total is 444 minutes.

questions.q: For a 4-digit number (greater than 1000), sum of the digits in the thousands, hundreds, and tens places is 15. Sum of the digits in the hundreds, tens, and units places is 16. Also, the digit in the tens place is 6 more than the digit in the units place. The difference between the largest and smallest possible value of the number is
questions.solution: Write digits a,b,c,d. Subtracting the two sum equations gives d=a+1. Also c=d+6=a+7 and b=8−2a. Valid digits allow a=1 or 2, giving 1682 and 2493. Difference is 811.

questions.q: Rahul starts on his journey at 5 pm at a constant speed so that he reaches his destination at 11 pm the same day. However, on his way, he stops for 20 minutes, and after that, increases his speed by 3 km per hour to reach on time. If he had stopped for 10 minutes more, he would have had to increase his speed by 5 km per hour to reach on time. His initial speed, in km per hour, was
questions.solution: Let original speed be v and remaining planned driving time at the stop be t hours. The 20-minute stop gives vt=(v+3)(t−1/3), so t=(v+3)/9. The 30-minute alternative gives t=(v+5)/10. Equating gives v=15 km/h.

questions.q: The rate of water flow through three pipes A, B and C are in the ratio 4 : 9 : 36. An empty tank can be filled up completely by pipe A in 15 hours. If all the three pipes are used simultaneously to fill up this empty tank, the time, in minutes, required to fill up the entire tank completely is nearest to
questions.solution: Set rates to 4,9,36 units/hour. Capacity =4×15=60 units. Combined time =60/49 hours =3600/49≈73.47 minutes, nearest to 73.

questions.q: If $$f(x)= (x^{2} + 3x)(x^{2}+ 3x+2)$$ then the sum of all real roots of the equation $$\sqrt{f(x)+1}= 9701$$, is
questions.solution: Put t=x²+3x. Then f(x)+1=(t+1)², so |t+1|=9701. The positive branch gives x²+3x−9700=0 with two real roots summing to −3. The negative branch has no real roots.

questions.q: For real values of x, the range of the function $$f(x)=\dfrac{2x-3}{2x^{2}+4x-6}$$ is
questions.solution: Set y=(2x−3)/(2x²+4x−6). The resulting quadratic in x has discriminant 4(16y²−10y+1). Real solutions require y≤1/8 or y≥1/2. The forbidden denominator roots x=1,−3 do not satisfy the rearranged equation, so this is the range.

questions.q: The sum of all the digits of the number $$(10^{50}+10^{25}-123)$$, is
questions.solution: Subtracting 123 leaves a long string of 9s followed by 877 below the 10²⁵ term, together with the leading 10⁵⁰ contribution. Direct integer expansion and digit summation give 221.

questions.q: A triangle ABC is formed with AB = AC = 50 cm and BC = 80 cm. Then, the sum of the lengths, in cm, of all three altitudes of the triangle ABC is
questions.solution: The altitude to base BC bisects 80 into 40 and 40. Its length is √(50²−40²)=30. Area is 1200 cm², so each altitude to a 50 cm side is 2×1200/50=48. Total =30+48+48=126.

questions.q: If $$\left( x^{2}+\frac{1}{x^{2}} \right)=25$$ and $$x>0$$, then the value of $$\left( x^{7}+\frac{1}{x^{7}} \right)$$ is
questions.solution: Let Sₙ=xⁿ+x⁻ⁿ. S₁=√27=3√3, S₂=25, and Sₙ=S₁Sₙ₋₁−Sₙ₋₂. Applying the recurrence up to n=7 yields S₇=44853√3.

questions.q: In a class of 150 students, 75 students chose physics, 111 students chose mathematics and 40 students chose chemistry. All students chose at least one of the three subjects and at least one student chose all three subjects. The number of students who chose both physics and chemistry is equal to the number of students who chose both chemistry and mathematics, and this is half the number of students who chose both physics and mathematics. The maximum possible number of students who chose physics but not mathematics, is
questions.solution: Let PC=CM=k, PM=2k, and triple intersection=t. Inclusion–exclusion gives 150=226−4k+t, so t=4k−76. At least one triple member forces k≥20. Physics without mathematics =75−2k, maximised at k=20 as 35. All resulting Venn regions are nonnegative.

questions.q: The sum of all possible real values of x for which $$\log_{x-3}{(x^{2}-9)}=\log_{x-3}{(x+1)}+2$$, is
questions.solution: The logarithm base requires x>3 and x≠4. Combining logs gives x²−9=(x+1)(x−3)². Cancel x−3, obtaining x+3=(x+1)(x−3), or x²−3x−6=0. Only (3+√33)/2 meets the domain.

questions.q: The average salary of 5 managers and 25 engineers in a company is 60000 rupees. If each of the managers received 20% salary increase while the salary of the engineers remained unchanged, the average salary of all 30 employees would have increased by 5%. The average salary, in rupees, of the engineers is
questions.solution: Total original salary is 30×60000=₹1800000. A 5% total increase is ₹90000, which is 20% of the managers’ original total. Managers originally earned ₹450000; engineers ₹1350000. Engineer average =1350000/25=₹54000.

questions.q: ABCD is a trapezium in which AB is parallel to DC, AD is perpendicular to AB, and AB = 3DC. If a circle inscribed in the trapezium touching all the sides has a radius of 3 cm , then the area, in sq. cm, of the trapezium is
questions.solution: The height between parallel tangents is twice the radius, 6. Let shorter base be d, longer base 3d. The legs are 6 and √(4d²+36). For a tangential quadrilateral, opposite-side sums agree: 4d=6+√(4d²+36), giving d=4. Area =(4+12)×6/2=48.

questions.q: If $$12^{12x}\times 4^{24x+12}\times 5^{2y}=8^{4z}\times 20 ^{12x} \times 243^{3x-6}$$, where x , y and z are natural numbers, then $$ x + y + z $$ equals
questions.solution: Compare prime exponents. Powers of 3 give 12x=15x−30, so x=10. Powers of 5 give 2y=12x, so y=60. Powers of 2 give 72x+24=12z+24x, so z=42. Total =112.

questions.q: In $$\triangle ABC$$, $$AB =AC= 12$$ cm and $$D$$ is a point on side $$BC$$ such that $$AD= 8$$ cm. If $$AD$$ is extended to a point $$E$$ such that $$\angle ACB = \angle AEB$$, then the length, in cm, of $$AE$$ is
questions.solution: The equal angles imply A,B,C,E lie on one circle. Intersecting chords at D give AD×DE=BD×DC. Since AB=AC=12 and AD=8, the isosceles-triangle identity gives BD×DC=12²−8²=80. Hence DE=10 and AE=18.

questions.q: Vessels A and B contain 60 litres of alcohol and 60 litres of water, respectively. A certain volume is taken out from A and poured into B. After stirring, the same volume is taken out from B and poured into A. If the resultant ratio of alcohol and water in A is 15 : 4, then the volume, in litres, initially taken out from A is
questions.solution: After transferring x litres each way, A contains water 60x/(60+x) and alcohol 3600/(60+x). Their ratio is 60/x=15/4, giving x=16 litres.

questions.q: The ratio of the number of coins in boxes A and B was 17:7. After 108 coins were shifted from box A to box B, this ratio became 37:20. The number of coins that needs to be shifted further from A to B, to make this ratio 1:1, is
questions.solution: Let original counts be 17k and 7k. After moving 108, 20(17k−108)=37(7k+108), giving k=76. The new counts differ by 544; moving half the difference, 272, makes them equal.

questions.q: Let p, q and r be three natural numbers such that their sum is 900, and r is a perfect square whose value lies between 150 and 500. If p is not less than 0.3q and not more than 0.7q, then the sum of the maximum and minimum possible values of p is
questions.solution: For a fixed square r, let s=900−r=p+q. The bounds give 3s/13≤p≤7s/17. The smallest p occurs at r=484, giving p=96; the largest at r=169 gives p=301. Their sum is 397.
